verdicts.command: Same probe as -4 F1 (hookprobe head with WithProcessGroup, base with New(); kill -KILL <pid> or kill -KILL -- -<pgid> of the hook, then ps -p <grandchild>)
verdicts.output: head: the grandchild survives both a kill of the hook pid and a kill of the hook's group ('S 3807828 /bin/sleep 41.3'; its pgid differs from the hook's pgid). base: the grandchild shares the hook's pgid, and a SIGKILL to the hook's group leaves it GONE. A SIGKILL to the hook pid alone leaves it alive on both. Real Claude Code was not killed.

Code read only, no run. group_unix.go:18 calls syscall.Kill(-cmd.Process.Pid, SIGKILL) by raw pid, not os.Process.Kill, which uses a pidfd. A race of exec.Cmd's context goroutine against Wait's reap plus pid reuse as a new pgid cannot be triggered deterministically. The kernel does not reuse a pid while it is still in use as a live pgid, so the window needs the whole group already reaped.
